key_insight: A thin high work-function metal interlayer between ITO and NiOx lowers the hole-injection barrier and strongly boosts all-inorganic PeLED luminance.
engineering_relevance: This is a scalable anode-engineering strategy that can improve charge injection and device brightness without changing the core perovskite stack.
method: Simulated device physics with drift-diffusion and Poisson equations in Setfos.
Inserted ultrathin high work-function metals between ITO and the hole transport layer.
Compared Au, Pd, and Pt interlayers for hole-injection improvement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that a 2 nm Au interlayer increased luminance by more than 18× in simulation, with similar trends for Pd and Pt.
watch_item: The result is simulation-based, so real-device performance, interlayer continuity, and fabrication reproducibility still need experimental validation.
paper_title: Boosting Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes Performance by Introducing High Work-function Metal Transition Layer
